runner_lane.benchmark: 72 Chocolate attended process: 25 retailers, 135 blocks walked. Coverage measured in ACV (doors as proxy), not banner count.

rules.text: Bright Data plus GitHub Actions, unattended, one domain per browser session. Attended Chrome is plan B only: mapping a new banner, bot-walled sites, the Costco warehouse tag, a broken recipe.

One run per new prospect. Monthly at most on retainer. No scheduled or daily pulls. The runner never writes to the database on its own; every landing goes through the mapper, a backup zip, and Steve's OK.

rules.rule: Kroger developer API is the primary route for Kroger banners
rules.text: (Steve, 2026-10-18, reversing 2026-10-14). The reading on record: Shelf Architect is a category-wide view across banners, and Kroger is one column in it. Kroger-specific cuts are made only when building a pitch to a Kroger buyer, which serves Kroger. Terms 4a (analysis targeting Kroger) is read as not applying to that use. Stored rows (Terms 5e) are a known exposure, accepted for small per-client datasets. If the key is ever revoked, the browser recipe is the fallback and nothing else in the process changes. Rows from this route carry the UPC and route runner-kroger-api.

One retailer table in the runner (slug, display name, id prefix) is the only source for retailer names and id prefixes, matched to what already exists in the database. Price history appends on an exact id match only. Anything looser is a merge plan that a person reviews; code never merges on a guess.
A row the runner cannot size is held, counted in the report, and never lands under a size-less id.

rules.rule: A card must name its product.
rules.text: On text-scraped banners a card is kept only if its own text contains the product name. Cards that fail are dropped and counted, because they were pairing one product's name with its neighbor's price.
Rows the runner did not see keep their last_pulled date and age. A run never deletes a row. Hand-pulled items outside the search terms stay as they are.

flavor, protein, priority and channel are never written by the runner. format (Frozen / Refrigerated / Shelf-stable) is the one exception: the runner fills it only where it is blank, never over a value Steve or a hand pull set, and records the evidence in format_source. Category comes from the client department.

(Steve, 2026-10-17). Every Stage 2 report ends with one coverage line: in-scope banners pulled, not found, attended pending; doors and ACV share covered; the biggest uncovered ACV named. Then one question: search more banners, or move on to the read. The run is not done until Steve answers. Never auto-expand.
Warehouse-local assortment, price_basis instacart_quote, roughly 15 percent over the warehouse tag. Pricing intel, not shelf price, and labeled that way on the row.

The v77 Instacart exception covered Steve's signed-in attended account. The runner uses no login: zip-pinned public storefront, lightest touch, no same-run retries, a verification wall ends that retailer for the run.

Backup zip to archives first, then one approval from Steve, then the SOP update and the rows land in the same sitting. The SOP will keep growing; a new rule is added here with a date and who set it. Coverage benchmark on record: 72 Chocolate's attended process, 25 retailers, 135 blocks walked. Coverage is measured in ACV, doors as the proxy until the per-banner ACV field exists, not in banner count.

rules.rule: Storage class on every row, wherever the source says it (v79).
rules.text: Order of evidence: (a) the retailer's own category (Kroger API categories), (b) explicit words in the product name or card (frozen, shelf-stable, can, jar, refrigerated, fresh), (c) the same brand and product already classified at another retailer, labeled same-product-elsewhere. If none speak, the field stays blank. The runner never guesses: a blank is a visible gap, a wrong flag poisons the price-per-oz read. Every report states rows flagged vs blank by retailer. Price comparisons and the thesis are always cut by storage class first.

rules.rule: Competitive pulls follow the competitors, not only the client markets (Steve, 2026-10-18).
rules.text: Each client has home markets and competitive markets. A banner is pulled in a market where it has doors: Albertsons in Boise, Jewel-Osco in Chicago, Safeway and King Soopers in Denver. Competitive markets are labeled on the client config and on every row's region. After every pull the runner compares the store it landed on with the market zip; a mismatch is reported as wrong market and is not mapped or landed (found 2026-10-18: Albertsons at a Denver zip pinned to an Idaho store).
List the home markets, then the competitive markets where the named competitors have shelf, and which banners have doors in each, before building blocks.

runner_lane.summary: Bright Data + GitHub Actions runner is the primary pull route; attended Chrome is plan B. Kroger developer API primary for Kroger banners (Steve 2026-10-18). Rules below are the v78 one-page SOP as approved. v79 (2026-10-18): format may be runner-filled where blank; storage class on every row; competitive markets; wrong-market check; intake step.

version_note: v79 2026-10-18: runner may fill format where blank (rule 8 amended), storage class rule, competitive markets and wrong-market check, new-client intake step. v78: runner_lane added (12 rules), Kroger API decision recorded, refresh_cadence caveat superseded for runner banners.
